laws.subtitle: Post-Austerity Investment Climate Law
laws.fullDescription: Capitalizes on Greece's return to investment grade credit ratings to attract foreign direct investment. The law creates the Enterprise Greece's enhanced mandate, establishes fast-track investment licensing for projects over €20 million, creates the Hellinikon mega-project framework for Athens's former airport, establishes green energy investment zones in the Aegean islands, and creates the Greece 2035 Investment Strategy.
laws.penalty: License withdrawal for investment projects failing promised employment targets; environmental liability
exceptions: Strategic national interest projects have confidential track
Tourism infrastructure has simplified environmental review

quiz.q: What former Athens facility is being redeveloped as part of Greece's Hellinikon mega-project?
quiz.explanation: The Hellinikon mega-project is transforming Athens's former Ellinikon airport into a massive mixed-use development including casino, marina, and residences.

laws.title: Investment Grade Recovery and Tourism Record
laws.subtitle: Greece Returns to Financial Stability After Crisis Decade
laws.fullDescription: Greece completed its return to investment-grade credit rating by all major rating agencies in 2024, marking the end of its decade-long recovery from the 2010-2018 debt crisis. Tourism records were broken with over 35 million visitors annually. GDP growth outpaced EU average, though inequality and brain drain remained concerns.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; fiscal surplus maintenance requirements
exceptions: Enhanced surveillance framework from ESM
Debt buyback program conditions

quiz.q: What did Greece achieve regarding credit ratings in 2024?
options: Investment grade status restored by all major agencies
quiz.explanation: Greece regained investment-grade credit ratings from all major agencies in 2024, marking the end of its decade-long recovery from the debt crisis.

laws.title: Attica Wildfires and Emergency Management Reform
laws.subtitle: Greece Modernizes Disaster Response After Major Fires
laws.fullDescription: Greece experienced devastating wildfires near Athens and in northern Greece in 2023, destroying thousands of hectares and forcing mass evacuations. The fires highlighted weaknesses in emergency management, firefighting capacity, and illegal development in fire-prone areas. The government invested in aerial firefighting capacity and reformed building codes.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for arson; enforcement of building codes in wildfire zones
exceptions: Traditional agricultural burning permits
Existing buildings given adaptation time

quiz.q: What major environmental challenge repeatedly threatens Greece near Athens?
quiz.explanation: Wildfires near Athens and in northern Greece have repeatedly threatened the country, leading to reforms in emergency management and firefighting capacity.

laws.title: Tempi Train Collision and Railway Safety Reform
laws.subtitle: Greece's Deadliest Train Crash Triggers Overhaul
laws.fullDescription: Greece's deadliest train disaster occurred in February 2023 when two passenger trains collided head-on near Tempi, killing 57 people, mostly university students. The crash exposed systemic failures in railway safety management. Mass protests demanded accountability, and criminal prosecutions followed along with comprehensive railway reform.
laws.penalty: Criminal prosecutions for negligence; railway operator regulations overhauled
exceptions: Operational safety protocols implementation timeline
EU railway regulation compliance

quiz.q: How many people died in Greece's 2023 Tempi train collision?
quiz.explanation: 57 people died in Greece's Tempi train collision in February 2023, mostly university students, triggering criminal prosecutions and comprehensive railway reform.

laws.title: Piraeus Port and Chinese Investment Controversy
laws.subtitle: COSCO Port Ownership Creates EU Security Concerns
laws.fullDescription: Greece's Piraeus port, operated by Chinese COSCO through a privatization, became a strategic flashpoint as the EU raised security concerns about Chinese control of a major European port. The Greek government navigated between maintaining the lucrative COSCO investment and meeting EU security requirements for sensitive infrastructure.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; EU security compliance requirements
exceptions: Existing concession agreement protections
FDI screening framework

quiz.q: Which Chinese company operates Piraeus port in Greece?
quiz.explanation: Chinese shipping giant COSCO operates the port of Piraeus following a privatization, creating EU security concerns about Chinese control of a major European port.

laws.title: Greek Economic Recovery and Tourism Overtourism
laws.subtitle: Greece rebounds from debt crisis but faces new sustainability challenges
laws.fullDescription: Greece has emerged from its decade-long debt crisis, exiting the final bailout program and regaining investment grade credit rating. Tourism, contributing 20%+ of GDP, drives recovery but creates overtourism in Santorini, Mykonos, and Athens. The government introduces daily visitor caps on Santorini and considers similar measures for the Acropolis. Greece balances economic reliance on tourism with quality of life for residents and preservation of historic sites.
laws.penalty: Unlicensed tourist accommodation and tour operators face increased fines and license revocation
exceptions: Off-season tourism actively encouraged with reduced landing fees
Agritourism in rural areas exempt from urban visitor restrictions

laws.title: Mega-Fires and Climate Change Threat to Mediterranean
laws.subtitle: Greece battles unprecedented wildfires as climate change intensifies
laws.fullDescription: Greece experienced devastating wildfires that became emblematic of Mediterranean climate change. The 2023 Evros wildfire was Europe's largest recorded, burning over 81,000 hectares. Fires near Athens and Rhodes required massive tourist evacuations. Greece is investing in aerial firefighting capacity and forest management. The fires reveal that Mediterranean ecology is being transformed by climate change, with regular megafires now expected rather than exceptional. Reforestation and adapted land management are priorities.
laws.penalty: Illegal construction in forests and fire-prone areas faces demolition orders
exceptions: Agricultural land adjacent to forests can continue farming with firebreak requirements
Existing permits for legally built structures maintained even in high-risk zones

laws.title: Offshore Wind Development and Energy Transition
laws.subtitle: Greece leverages Aegean winds for renewable energy leadership
laws.fullDescription: Greece is developing major offshore wind projects in the Aegean Sea, which has some of Europe's best wind resources. The country aims to have 5 GW of offshore wind by 2030. Greece also has excellent solar resources and is building interconnectors with neighboring countries to export renewable electricity. The energy transition is partly driven by reducing Greece's dependence on imported fossil fuels that drain foreign exchange. New offshore wind licensing rounds have attracted major international developers.
laws.penalty: Offshore wind developers must comply with maritime spatial planning and environmental assessment requirements
exceptions: Archaeological surveys required before seabed works; significant finds can delay projects
Fishery protection zones require modified foundations in certain areas

quiz.q: How much offshore wind capacity is Greece targeting by 2030?
quiz.explanation: Greece targets 5 GW of offshore wind capacity by 2030, leveraging the Aegean Sea's excellent wind resources — one of Europe's best — as part of its broader clean energy transition.

laws.title: Shipping Empire and Greek Oligarch Maritime Power
laws.subtitle: Greece controls the world's largest private shipping fleet
laws.fullDescription: Greek shipowners control the world's largest merchant fleet by tonnage — approximately 20% of global shipping capacity. Families like Onassis, Niarchos, Angelopoulos, and Latsis built global empires. The fleet is managed mostly from Piraeus and Monaco but registered in Panama and Liberia for tax and regulatory advantages. Greek shipping provides significant services income for Greece's balance of payments. The Greek shipping community is politically influential and has largely operated outside Greek tax jurisdiction through historical arrangements.
laws.penalty: Greek-registered shipping companies must comply with Greek tax obligations since recent tax reform
exceptions: Tonnage tax regime for Greek-flagged ships provides alternative to standard corporate income tax
Legacy arrangements for some shipping families phased out under EU pressure on tax privileges

quiz.q: What percentage of global shipping capacity do Greek shipowners control?
quiz.explanation: Greek shipowners control approximately 20% of global merchant shipping by tonnage — the largest share of any national group — making Greek shipping one of the world's most significant maritime powers.

laws.title: Post-Austerity Recovery and Tourism Dependency Risks
laws.subtitle: Greece rebuilding after a decade of economic crisis
laws.fullDescription: Greece experienced one of the most severe debt crises of any developed economy, with three successive bailout programs totaling over €300 billion, deep austerity measures, GDP falling by about 25%, and unemployment reaching 27%. After exiting the bailout programs in 2018, Greece has achieved a remarkable economic recovery, returning to growth and achieving primary budget surpluses. The economy has benefited enormously from record tourism — Greece received over 32 million visitors in 2023, making tourism a pillar of recovery. However, heavy dependence on tourism creates vulnerability to external shocks. Greece also faces persistent structural issues: a large shadow economy, brain drain of educated young Greeks, an inefficient public sector, and demographic decline. The government has pursued investment attraction through tax incentives and digital nomad programs. Relations with Turkey remain a persistent source of tension.
laws.penalty: Tax evasion carries criminal penalties; Greece has implemented significant improvements in tax collection as part of post-crisis reforms
exceptions: Some island communities have special VAT rates to support economic activity

quiz.q: How much did Greek GDP fall during the debt crisis period?
quiz.explanation: Greek GDP fell by approximately 25% during the debt crisis — one of the most severe economic contractions of any developed economy in recent history, accompanied by 27% unemployment at its peak.

laws.title: Wildfire Crisis and Climate Adaptation Emergency
laws.subtitle: Greece experiencing increasingly catastrophic wildfire seasons
laws.fullDescription: Greece has experienced devastating wildfires in recent years, with the 2021 fires burning over 1,000 square kilometers on Evia island — the country's second-largest island — and the 2023 fires near Alexandroupoli being among Europe's largest in recorded history. Climate change has extended fire season, increased temperatures, and created more extreme drought conditions that elevate fire risk. The 2023 fires near Rhodes forced mass tourist evacuation from beaches by boat — extraordinary scenes that damaged Greece's tourism reputation. Greece has faced criticism for inadequate forest management, insufficient fire preparedness, and illegal construction in forested areas. The aftermath reveals governance challenges: land use management failures, insufficient reforestation, and corruption that allowed building in protected areas. Greece is implementing forest management reforms and investing in firefighting capacity.
laws.penalty: Illegal burning and arson in forests carry criminal penalties; unauthorized construction in forest areas can result in demolition orders
exceptions: Some traditional agricultural activities involving prescribed burning have historical tolerance

quiz.q: What extraordinary event during Greece's 2023 wildfires damaged the country's tourism reputation?
options: Smoke covered Athens for three weeks during peak summer
Mass tourist evacuation from Rhodes beaches by boat during fires
A major wildfire destroyed the ancient Acropolis complex
Airport closures stranded thousands of tourists for a week
quiz.explanation: During the 2023 Rhodes wildfires, mass tourist evacuations from beaches by boat created extraordinary images that were broadcast globally — severely damaging Greece's tourism reputation during the peak summer season.

laws.title: Tourism Overcrowding and Resident Backlash
laws.subtitle: Greek islands struggle with overtourism sustainability crisis
laws.fullDescription: Greece has experienced record tourism numbers, but residents of Santorini, Mykonos and Acropolis areas have begun protesting overtourism. Santorini capped cruise ship arrivals. The Acropolis introduced timed ticketing. Athens neighborhoods near the Acropolis suffer from Airbnb-driven housing shortages. Greece debates how to balance the tourism industry that provides 25% of GDP with quality of life for residents. Fires and water shortages in tourist-heavy areas also reflect environmental pressure.
laws.penalty: Cruise ship docking limits enforced at selected islands; fines for unlicensed short-term rentals
exceptions: Licensed tourist businesses operate within quota systems
Island communities retain local authority over some restrictions

quiz.q: What percentage of Greek GDP does tourism provide?
quiz.explanation: Tourism provides approximately 25% of Greek GDP, making overtourism both an existential economic issue and a quality-of-life crisis for residents of popular destinations.

laws.title: Wildfires and Climate Adaptation Crisis
laws.subtitle: Record fires destroy forests and tourist areas
laws.fullDescription: Greece experienced some of its worst wildfires in recorded history in recent years, with massive blazes burning through the Evros region, Attica near Athens and the island of Rhodes in 2023. Climate change has extended the fire season and intensified fire behavior. Tourist evacuations from Rhodes became images seen worldwide. Greece has struggled with underfunded fire services, illegal construction in forests and inadequate land use planning that allows urban-forest interfaces where fire risk is highest. Recovery and adaptation investment has been significant.
laws.penalty: Illegal construction in burned forest areas prohibited; reforestation of burned areas required with building bans for many years
exceptions: Pre-existing legal structures retain rights even after fire
Emergency accommodation for evacuated residents handled through crisis funds

quiz.q: Which Greek island became internationally known for tourist evacuations during the 2023 wildfire season?
quiz.explanation: Rhodes became internationally known when its 2023 wildfires forced the evacuation of thousands of tourists from beach resorts, creating dramatic images that circled the globe and highlighted Greece's wildfire crisis.

laws.title: Predator Spyware Scandal
laws.subtitle: Greece uses commercial surveillance software against journalists and politicians
laws.fullDescription: Greece was exposed using Predator spyware developed by Cytrox to monitor journalists, politicians and foreign officials. The scandal implicated Prime Minister Mitsotakis's government, with his own nephew being targeted along with opposition leaders. Greece became one of the most prominent European cases of domestic spyware abuse. The European Parliament investigated EU member state spyware use. Greece's case demonstrated that commercial surveillance software had spread beyond authoritarian governments to nominal EU democracies.
laws.penalty: Illegal surveillance subject to criminal prosecution; parliamentary investigations launched but prosecutions rare
exceptions: Legitimate law enforcement wiretapping requires judicial authorization
National security surveillance under separate legal framework

quiz.q: What commercial spyware was Greece found to have used against journalists and politicians?
quiz.explanation: Greece was exposed using Predator spyware developed by Cytrox to monitor journalists, politicians and foreign officials, becoming one of the most prominent European cases of domestic surveillance software abuse within an EU democracy.

laws.title: Elgin Marbles Repatriation Campaign
laws.subtitle: Greece's decades-long campaign to recover Parthenon sculptures
laws.fullDescription: Greece has campaigned for over 40 years for the UK to return the Parthenon sculptures (Elgin Marbles) taken by Lord Elgin in the early 19th century and held at the British Museum. Momentum increased as PM Mitsotakis cancelled a scheduled meeting with Rishi Sunak over the issue in 2023. The British Museum Act prevents deaccessioning objects from the collection. Some partial loan arrangements have been discussed. The case has become a broader debate about colonial-era acquisition of cultural objects from their countries of origin.
laws.penalty: UK law prevents British Museum from returning collection items; legal reform would be needed for permanent return
exceptions: Long-term loans not counted as deaccessioning under museum law
Bilateral cultural partnerships can facilitate temporary display in Athens

quiz.q: What British law prevents the British Museum from returning the Elgin Marbles permanently to Greece?
quiz.explanation: The British Museum Act prevents the British Museum from permanently deaccessioning items from its collection, including the Parthenon sculptures taken by Lord Elgin—requiring primary legislation to change, which the UK government has been unwilling to pursue.

laws.title: National Climate Law and Lignite Exit
laws.subtitle: Mediterranean Climate Frontline
laws.fullDescription: Greece's 2022 National Climate Law (Law 4936/2022) sets binding targets for 55% emissions reduction by 2030 and climate neutrality by 2050. Greece accelerated its exit from lignite (brown coal) which had powered 60% of electricity, announcing the closure of all lignite plants by 2028. Greece is severely impacted by climate change: the 2021 wildfires burned 125,000 hectares including on Evia island; the 2023 floods in Thessaly destroyed crops; and the Mediterranean is warming faster than the global average. Greece invests heavily in solar and wind power.
laws.penalty: Fines for violating emission standards; permit denial for high-emission projects
exceptions: Lignite phase-out subject to just transition provisions for Western Macedonia region
Islands under special energy security framework

laws.title: Greek National Health System (ESY)
laws.subtitle: Austerity and Healthcare Crisis
laws.fullDescription: Greece's National Health System (ESY), created in 1983, provides universal free healthcare funded through taxation and social insurance contributions. The 2010 financial crisis and subsequent EU-IMF austerity severely damaged Greece's healthcare: spending was cut 30%+, hospitals lost staff and supplies, and emigration of doctors accelerated. Infant mortality temporarily increased and medicine shortages emerged. Greece has since partially recovered, and EOPYY (the national health insurer) was streamlined. Greece has remarkably high life expectancy attributed to Mediterranean diet and lifestyle.
laws.penalty: EOPYY contributions mandatory for workers; healthcare rights legally established; pharmaceutical pricing regulations
exceptions: Uninsured residents can access emergency care
EU citizens with EHIC card covered

laws.title: Greek Labor Laws and Austerity Recovery
laws.subtitle: From Austerity Cuts to 6-Day Week
laws.fullDescription: Greece's labor laws were significantly weakened during the 2010-2018 austerity period — minimum wage was cut 22% (from €751 to €586/month), collective bargaining was undermined, and worker protections reduced. Since austerity ended, Greece has gradually restored the minimum wage to €830/month (2024) and beyond. In a controversial 2024 decision, Greece legalized a 6-day workweek (up to 48 hours) for some industrial and service sectors — argued as needed for competitiveness but criticized by unions as regression. Greece still has high youth unemployment (20%+) and significant emigration of young workers.
laws.penalty: Labor inspection fines for violations; minimum wage enforcement; illegal dismissal: compensation via courts
exceptions: 6-day week requires specific sector authorization
Part-time workers under proportional protections

laws.title: Greek Free University Education
laws.subtitle: PISA Challenges and Brain Drain
laws.fullDescription: Greece provides free university education at public AEI (Higher Education Institutions). Admission is through national Panhellenic Exams — extremely stressful, with a multi-billion euro private tutoring industry (frontistiria) preparing students. Greece's PISA scores are among the lowest in the EU, particularly in mathematics. The 2010-2018 austerity program cut education spending significantly. Brain drain is severe — over 400,000 educated Greeks emigrated during the crisis decade. Greece's private education market is large despite constitutional ambiguity about private universities (partially resolved in 2024 with a controversial private university bill).
laws.penalty: National Panhellenic Exam results legally binding for admission; university research quality monitored by HAHE; teacher certification required
exceptions: Military academies under separate Defense Ministry
Church-affiliated theological seminaries under distinct framework

laws.title: EU-Turkey Deal and Island Hotspot System
laws.subtitle: Greece's role as Europe's main Eastern Mediterranean entry point
laws.fullDescription: Greece has been Europe's primary entry point for migrants from Turkey crossing the Aegean Sea. The EU-Turkey Deal (2016) — paying Turkey €6 billion to contain migration — dramatically reduced crossings but has been contested over Turkey's compliance. Greece operates 'hotspot' reception centers on Aegean islands (Lesbos, Chios, Samos) that have been chronically overcrowded and criticized for inhumane conditions. The Moria camp fire (2020) left 12,000 people homeless. Greece has also been accused of illegal pushbacks of migrants in the Aegean Sea.
laws.penalty: Irregular entry to Greece is a misdemeanor punishable by up to 3 months jail; human smuggling carries 5+ year sentences; Greek authorities conducting illegal pushbacks face EU legal proceedings (though pushbacks continue)
exceptions: Recognized refugees receive international protection status
EU citizens have unrestricted residence
Migrants with family members in other EU countries may be transferred under Dublin Regulation
laws.sourceLabel: Greece Asylum Law and EU-Turkey Deal Implementation

quiz.q: The 2016 EU-Turkey Deal gave Turkey approximately how much funding in exchange for containing migration flows?
quiz.explanation: The March 2016 EU-Turkey Statement (commonly called the EU-Turkey Deal) committed €6 billion in EU funds to Turkey in exchange for Turkey containing irregular migration to Greece, taking back migrants who crossed to Greece, and accepting one Syrian refugee from EU for each Syrian returned to Turkey.

laws.title: Drug Law and Cannabis Decriminalization
laws.subtitle: Greece's evolving drug policy and cannabis reform
laws.fullDescription: Greece's drug law (Law 4139/2013) classifies drugs into three categories with different penalties. Greece decriminalized cannabis possession for personal use: up to 10g can be charged as a minor offense (up to 5 months jail) rather than full criminal prosecution; in practice, small amounts are often diverted to treatment. Greece legalized medical cannabis in 2017 and became a significant cannabis cultivation and export country (to EU and beyond). Drug trafficking carries 5-20 years. Greece has major drug transit concerns as a Mediterranean entry point.
laws.penalty: Cannabis personal possession: minor offense with diversion to treatment; trafficking up to 10 years; trafficking to minors: 5-20 years; heroin/cocaine possession for personal use: minor offense possible; large-scale trafficking: 20 years to life
exceptions: Personal use possession may be diverted to drug courts/treatment
Medical cannabis and hemp cultivation regulated and exported
Harm reduction services funded by government

quiz.q: Following cannabis legalization for medical use in 2017, Greece became notable in Europe for what related industry?
options: Creating the world's largest cannabis social club network
Becoming a significant legal cannabis cultivator and exporter to EU countries
Opening the first European cannabis coffee shop chain
Developing cannabis-based pharmaceutical exports to the US
quiz.explanation: After legalizing medical cannabis in 2017, Greece invested heavily in licensed cannabis cultivation, becoming one of Europe's largest producers and exporters of medical cannabis to pharmaceutical companies and dispensaries across the EU.

laws.title: Same-Sex Marriage Legalized in 2024
laws.subtitle: Greece became the first Orthodox-majority country to legalize same-sex marriage
laws.fullDescription: Greece legalized same-sex marriage on February 15, 2024, becoming the first country with a predominantly Greek Orthodox Christian population to do so. The law was passed by parliament 176-76 and signed by President Katerina Sakellaropoulou. Same-sex married couples also gained equal parenting rights including recognition on birth certificates. This was a significant shift, as Greece had only introduced civil partnerships for same-sex couples in 2015. The Greek Orthodox Church strongly opposed the law.
laws.penalty: Anti-discrimination laws cover sexual orientation in employment; hate crime provisions were strengthened alongside the marriage law
exceptions: The Greek Orthodox Church is not required to perform or recognize same-sex marriages

quiz.q: What distinction did Greece hold when legalizing same-sex marriage in 2024?
quiz.explanation: Greece became the first country with a predominantly Greek Orthodox Christian population to legalize same-sex marriage, passing the law in February 2024 despite strong opposition from the Greek Orthodox Church.

laws.title: Predator Spyware Scandal and Press Freedom Concerns
laws.subtitle: Greece was rocked by a 2022 spyware scandal involving surveillance of journalists
laws.fullDescription: Greece's constitution (Article 14) protects freedom of the press. Greece was deeply shaken by the 2022 'Predator' scandal in which journalist Thanasis Koukakis and others were found to have been targeted with Predator spyware — linked to a company connected to businessman Tal Dilian. The government's initial response was criticized as inadequate. Greece has criminal defamation laws. The government of Kyriakos Mitsotakis faced questions about its role in the surveillance. Greece has a tradition of yellow journalism and concentrated media ownership. RSF has ranked Greece among the lower tier of EU members for press freedom.
laws.penalty: Criminal defamation laws apply; spyware surveillance of journalists occurred in 2022; press licensing does not exist but concentration is significant
exceptions: EU member status requires compliance with press freedom norms

quiz.q: What scandal severely damaged Greece's press freedom reputation in 2022?
quiz.explanation: In 2022, Greece was rocked by the 'Predator' spyware scandal in which journalist Thanasis Koukakis and others were found to have been targeted with sophisticated commercial spyware — a revelation that damaged the government's reputation and raised serious press freedom concerns in an EU member state.

laws.title: Hellenic DPA and Predator Spyware GDPR Implications
laws.subtitle: Greece's HDPA handles data protection enforcement while Predator spyware raised surveillance concerns
laws.fullDescription: Greece's Hellenic Data Protection Authority (HDPA) enforces GDPR. The Predator spyware scandal (2022) involved surveillance tools used to monitor Greek citizens including journalists and politicians — raising GDPR concerns about state surveillance. HDPA investigated the Predator case. Greece's Authority for Communication Security and Privacy (ADAE) oversees communications security. Greek courts have addressed social media platform liability. Greece implements EU DSA through EETT (telecommunications regulator). The Predator case led to parliamentary investigations but full accountability remains elusive.
laws.penalty: HDPA GDPR fines; Predator spyware investigation; ADAE communications security oversight
exceptions: National security surveillance is regulated separately from commercial data protection

quiz.q: How did the Predator spyware scandal in Greece intersect with digital privacy law?
options: It was unrelated to privacy law
HDPA investigated whether state use of spyware on citizens violated GDPR privacy rights
It led to new anti-encryption laws
Greece was fined by the EU for Predator use
quiz.explanation: The 2022 Predator spyware scandal in Greece raised direct GDPR questions when surveillance tools were found to have monitored journalists, politicians, and private citizens — leading HDPA to investigate whether state actors' use of commercial spyware violated GDPR privacy rights.

laws.title: Post-Crisis Banking Reforms & Capital Controls Aftermath
laws.subtitle: Greece rebuilt banking supervision after the 2015 capital control crisis
laws.fullDescription: During Greece's 2015 debt crisis, the government imposed capital controls limiting ATM withdrawals to €60/day and banning transfers abroad. Though capital controls were fully lifted by September 2019, their legacy shaped strict banking rules. The Bank of Greece (Τράπεζα της Ελλάδος) and the Hellenic Capital Market Commission supervise banks and securities firms. Greece implemented mandatory e-invoicing (myDATA) for all businesses in 2021 and offers a 30% tax discount on card/electronic payments exceeding 30% of declared income. Cash transactions above €500 must be made electronically between professionals.
laws.penalty: Cash transactions exceeding €500 between professionals: fines up to €1,500; e-invoicing violations: fines of €100-500 per invoice; unlicensed financial services: up to €2 million
exceptions: Agricultural sector retains some higher cash transaction limits
Emergency medical payments may be cash regardless of amount
Tourists from outside EU have modified electronic payment requirements

quiz.q: What was the daily ATM withdrawal limit during Greece's 2015 capital controls?
quiz.explanation: During Greece's 2015 banking crisis, the government imposed capital controls limiting citizens to €60 per day in ATM withdrawals and banning most international transfers.

laws.title: EFET Food Authority & Greek PDO Product Protection
laws.subtitle: Greece protects iconic products like feta cheese and Kalamata olives through EU designations
laws.fullDescription: Greece's Food Safety Authority (EFET) enforces food safety law, implementing EU regulations. Greece fought and won major EU battles over food designation protection: Feta cheese won exclusive PDO status in 2002 after years of legal battles with Denmark and other EU countries, meaning only cheese made in Greece from Greek sheep's and goat's milk using traditional methods can be called Feta. Other Greek PDO products include Kalamata olives, Corinthian currants, Mastiha (mastic gum from Chios), and Agiorgitiko wine. Greece has strict rules for olive oil — the country produces approximately 80% of EU extra virgin olive oil. EFET inspects restaurants, food processors, and markets, issuing public online lists of violators.
laws.penalty: EFET violations: fines up to €30,000; PDO fraud (e.g., selling Danish cheese as Feta): EU-level enforcement; olive oil adulteration: criminal prosecution; public EFET violation list publication
exceptions: Traditional taverna food preparation has modified HACCP implementation
Greek Easter lamb preparation in religious contexts has cultural exemptions
Small-scale island food producers have simplified transportation and hygiene rules

quiz.q: What was the outcome of Greece's EU legal battle over Feta cheese protection?
options: Greece lost — Feta remains a generic term in the EU
Greece won in 2002 — Feta is now exclusive PDO status for Greek-made sheep/goat milk cheese
A compromise: EU countries can use 'Feta-style' but not 'Feta'
Pending — the EU Court of Justice has not yet ruled
quiz.explanation: Greece won EU-wide Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) for Feta cheese in 2002, after legal challenges from Denmark and other countries. Only cheese made in specific Greek regions from Greek sheep's (and up to 30% goat's) milk using traditional methods can be sold as 'Feta' in the EU.

laws.title: Greece Animal Welfare Law and Stray Dog Crisis
laws.subtitle: Greece struggles to enforce welfare laws amid large stray populations
laws.fullDescription: Greece's Law 4830/2021 is its most recent comprehensive animal welfare reform, following years of inadequate enforcement. Greece has a significant stray animal problem — estimated hundreds of thousands of stray dogs and cats, partly due to illegal abandonment during economic crises. The 2021 law requires all companion animals to be microchipped and registered, mandates sterilization programs, prohibits abandonment, and creates a national stray animal registry. Animal cruelty became a more serious criminal offense. Greece also reformed its approach to stray management from lethal control to TNR (trap-neuter-return). Enforcement remains a challenge — local capacity and resources are limited.
laws.penalty: Animal cruelty: up to 10 years imprisonment (increased dramatically in 2021 reform); abandonment: up to 1 year; organized animal cruelty: up to 10 years
exceptions: Livestock farming under EU standards
Licensed hunting
Scientific research
Traditional cultural events

quiz.q: What dramatic change did Greece's 2021 animal welfare reform make to cruelty penalties?
options: It reduced penalties to focus on education
It increased maximum imprisonment for animal cruelty to up to 10 years
It transferred cruelty cases to civil courts
quiz.explanation: Greece's 2021 Law 4830 dramatically increased animal cruelty penalties — raising maximum imprisonment to up to 10 years in serious cases, a significant escalation in Greece's approach to animal welfare enforcement.

laws.title: Greece — Civil Partnership and 2024 Same-Sex Marriage
laws.subtitle: Greece legalized same-sex marriage in February 2024
laws.fullDescription: Greece legalized same-sex marriage in February 2024 — becoming the first Orthodox-majority country to do so. Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis's conservative New Democracy party sponsored the bill, which passed with cross-party support despite opposition from the Greek Orthodox Church. Greece had civil partnerships (σύμφωνο συμβίωσης) since 2015 for both same-sex and opposite-sex couples. Greek divorce law requires either 6-month consensual separation or 2-year unilateral separation. Default property regime: community of acquired assets. Greek family courts handle child custody (γονική μέριμνα) with increasing preference for joint custody. Greece has strong inheritance rights for surviving spouses.
laws.penalty: Civil enforcement through πρωτοδικεία (first-instance courts); alimentary support enforced by courts; property seizure for persistent non-payment
exceptions: Προγαμιαία σύμβαση (prenuptial agreement)
Pre-marital property retained
Σύμφωνο συμβίωσης (civil partnership) as alternative

quiz.q: What historic distinction did Greece achieve in February 2024 regarding same-sex marriage?
options: Greece became the last EU country to ban same-sex marriage
Greece became the first Orthodox-majority country in the world to legalize same-sex marriage
Greece introduced mandatory religious blessing for all marriages
Greece made marriage optional — eliminating civil requirements
quiz.explanation: Greece's February 2024 same-sex marriage legalization was historic — it made Greece the first Orthodox Christian-majority country in the world to legally recognize same-sex marriage. The bill was sponsored by the conservative New Democracy party and passed despite strong opposition from the Greek Orthodox Church.

laws.title: Greece Astikos Kodikas & Housing Crisis Response
laws.subtitle: Post-crisis property rights and rental regulations
laws.fullDescription: Greece's Astikos Kodikas (Civil Code) and rental law (Law 1703/1987, revised) govern property rights. Following the 2010-2018 debt crisis, hundreds of thousands of properties were foreclosed and transferred to bad-loan funds. Law 4816/2021 extended mortgage protection for primary residences. Greece also faces a short-term rental crisis with Airbnb proliferating, particularly in Athens and Thessaloniki. Law 4276/2014 on short-term rentals was strengthened in 2024 to require registration and limit days per year. A major issue is property tax (ENFIA) reform, recalculated on property values in 2022.
laws.penalty: Mortgage protection for primary residence under EUR 250,000 in value; illegal Airbnb: fine up to EUR 5,000
exceptions: Post-crisis primary residence protection laws prevent foreclosure below thresholds
ENFIA property tax recalculated on 2022 market values

quiz.q: What major event between 2010-2018 led to widespread property foreclosures in Greece?
options: The EU-IMF debt crisis and austerity measures
quiz.explanation: Greece's debt crisis (2010-2018) required EU-IMF bailout programs with austerity conditions, leading to massive unemployment, widespread mortgage defaults, and hundreds of thousands of property foreclosures by bad-debt funds.

laws.title: Greece Consumer Protection Law & GCCRF
laws.subtitle: Consumer rights and market inspection authority
laws.fullDescription: Greece's consumer protection is governed by Law 2251/1994 (amended), implementing EU consumer directives including 14-day distance withdrawal, 2-year warranty, and prohibition of unfair commercial practices. The GCCRF (General Directorate for Consumer Protection and Market Supervision) enforces consumer law. The Consumer Ombudsman (Synigoros tou Katanaloti) handles individual complaints and can issue non-binding recommendations. Greek consumer associations (EKPIZO) are active litigants. Post-financial crisis, Greece has strengthened enforcement against overcharging, price gouging, and misleading labeling. Greek courts have dealt with significant cases on bank fee transparency and telecom consumer rights.
laws.penalty: Consumer law violation: fines and market withdrawal of products; distance withdrawal: 14 days full refund
exceptions: Consumer Ombudsman handles individual consumer complaints
Post-financial crisis enforcement strengthened against price gouging

quiz.q: What is the role of Greece's Consumer Ombudsman (Synigoros tou Katanaloti)?
options: Handling individual consumer complaints and issuing non-binding recommendations
quiz.explanation: Greece's Consumer Ombudsman (Synigoros tou Katanaloti) handles individual consumer complaints and mediates between consumers and businesses, issuing non-binding recommendations — a free, fast alternative to court that many businesses comply with to avoid formal regulatory action.

laws.title: Schengen External Border Control
laws.subtitle: Greece as EU's frontline migration entry point
laws.fullDescription: Greece serves as a primary external border of the Schengen Area, obligating it to enforce EU border regulations under Regulation (EU) 2016/399. The country operates border surveillance along its Aegean Sea coastline and land border with Turkey. Frontex, the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, maintains a significant presence in Greece to assist with border management. Unauthorized crossing constitutes a criminal offense under Greek Law 3907/2011, which also governs asylum procedures.
laws.penalty: Detention up to 18 months; deportation for irregular entry
exceptions: Recognized asylum seekers
EU citizens and family members
Holders of valid Schengen visas

quiz.q: Which EU agency assists Greece with Schengen border management?
quiz.explanation: Frontex, the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, maintains a major presence in Greece to support Schengen external border enforcement.

laws.title: Capital Controls Legacy Framework
laws.subtitle: Post-2015 financial crisis banking restrictions
laws.fullDescription: During the 2015 debt crisis, Greece imposed capital controls limiting cash withdrawals to €60 per day and restricting international transfers. While formal capital controls were lifted in September 2019, residual monitoring frameworks under Bank of Greece supervision remain in place. The controls were established under Emergency Law 4350/2015 and caused significant disruption to businesses and individuals. Greece completed its third bailout program in August 2018 under the European Stability Mechanism, with ongoing fiscal surveillance continuing through 2022.
laws.penalty: Fines up to €50,000 for illegal capital transfers; criminal prosecution possible
exceptions: Medical emergency payments
Essential import payments
Approved business transactions

quiz.q: When were Greece's formal capital controls officially lifted?
quiz.explanation: Greece's formal capital controls, imposed during the 2015 debt crisis, were officially lifted in September 2019 after the country stabilized its financial system.

laws.title: Austerity-Era Labor Market Reforms
laws.subtitle: Structural changes to employment law post-2010
laws.fullDescription: Greece enacted sweeping labor market reforms between 2010 and 2015 under EU-IMF bailout conditionality, fundamentally altering employment protections. Minimum wage was cut by 22% (32% for youth under 25) in 2012, though restored and increased by subsequent governments. Collective bargaining agreements were weakened, allowing firm-level contracts to override sector-wide agreements. Law 4093/2012 and subsequent legislation reduced severance pay entitlements and extended probationary periods, transforming one of Europe's most protected labor markets.
laws.penalty: Administrative fines for employers violating reformed labor codes; back-pay obligations
exceptions: Civil servants under separate statutory framework
Employees covered by grandfathered collective agreements
Disabled workers with enhanced protections

quiz.q: By what percentage was Greece's minimum wage cut for workers under 25 in 2012?
quiz.explanation: The 2012 austerity measures cut the minimum wage by 22% for adults and 32% for workers under 25, as part of EU-IMF bailout conditions.

laws.title: Tourism Infrastructure and Airport Tax Law
laws.subtitle: Passenger fees and tourism levy regulations
laws.fullDescription: Greece imposes a Climate Crisis Resilience Tax on tourist accommodation introduced in 2024, ranging from €0.50 to €10 per night depending on property category and season. Airport departure taxes are governed by Law 2338/1995 as amended, with different charges for domestic, intra-EU, and international flights. The Hellenic Civil Aviation Authority oversees airport operations and safety compliance. Greece's tourism sector, contributing approximately 25% of GDP, is subject to special licensing requirements under Presidential Decree 43/2002 for hospitality businesses.
laws.penalty: Fines up to €10,000 for accommodation operators failing to collect and remit tourism taxes
exceptions: Children under 2 years
Transit passengers not leaving airport
Diplomatic personnel with accreditation

quiz.q: Approximately what percentage of Greece's GDP does the tourism sector contribute?
quiz.explanation: Tourism contributes approximately 25% of Greece's GDP, making it a critical sector subject to extensive regulation and taxation.

laws.title: Short-Term Rental Registration Requirement
laws.subtitle: Airbnb and holiday let registration under AADE
laws.fullDescription: Greece requires all short-term rental properties to be registered with the Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE) and obtain a Registration Number displayed in all listings. Law 4472/2017 established the framework for short-term rental taxation, with income subject to progressive rates starting at 15%. Property owners must declare rental income through the myProperty digital platform. Municipalities in major tourist areas like Santorini and Mykonos have additional local restrictions on new short-term rental licenses to address housing availability concerns.
laws.penalty: Fines of €5,000 per unregistered property; additional tax penalties for undeclared income
exceptions: Properties rented fewer than 60 days per year in some municipalities
Owner-occupied rooms below certain size thresholds
Properties subject to long-term lease agreements

quiz.q: What platform must Greek property owners use to declare short-term rental income?
quiz.explanation: Greek property owners must declare short-term rental income through the myProperty digital platform operated by the AADE tax authority.

laws.title: Coastal Zone Protection Law
laws.subtitle: Construction restrictions in Greece's shoreline areas
laws.fullDescription: Greek Law 2971/2001 establishes strict protection zones along the country's 16,000 km coastline, prohibiting most construction within 50 meters of the sea (100 meters in unplanned areas). The law aims to preserve public access to beaches and prevent illegal encroachment by private development. The Central Archaeological Council also has jurisdiction over coastal areas near ancient sites. Enforcement has historically been inconsistent, and the 2023 Mati wildfire disaster prompted renewed scrutiny of illegal coastal construction that blocked evacuation routes.
laws.penalty: Demolition orders for illegal structures; fines up to €500,000; criminal charges for developers
exceptions: Pre-existing legal structures grandfathered before 1967
Port and harbor infrastructure
Public beach facilities approved by state

quiz.q: What is the standard coastal construction exclusion zone under Greek Law 2971/2001?
quiz.explanation: Greek law prohibits most construction within 50 meters of the sea (100 meters in unplanned areas) to protect public coastal access.

laws.title: Debt Restructuring and Private Insolvency Law
laws.subtitle: Post-crisis personal bankruptcy framework
laws.fullDescription: Greece enacted Law 4738/2020, the "Debt Settlement and Second Chance" law, establishing a comprehensive framework for personal and business insolvency modeled on EU Directive 2019/1023. The law created an out-of-court debt settlement mechanism allowing debtors to restructure obligations to banks, tax authorities, and social security funds simultaneously. A new electronic insolvency platform facilitates applications and creditor negotiations. The reform was a key requirement of post-bailout fiscal surveillance, replacing the fragmented pre-crisis Katseli Law framework that had left hundreds of thousands of cases unresolved in courts.
laws.penalty: Fraudulent concealment of assets during insolvency: criminal charges and loss of discharge rights
exceptions: Debts from criminal fines
Child support obligations
Recent tax debts less than 1 year old

quiz.q: Which EU directive did Greece's 2020 insolvency law (4738/2020) implement?
quiz.explanation: Greek Law 4738/2020 implemented EU Directive 2019/1023 on restructuring and insolvency, creating a modernized second-chance framework.

laws.title: GDPR Implementation and Data Protection Authority
laws.subtitle: Greek personal data protection under Law 4624/2019
laws.fullDescription: Greece implemented the EU General Data Protection Regulation through Law 4624/2019, establishing the Hellenic Data Protection Authority (HDPA) as the national supervisory authority. The HDPA has issued significant fines against major organizations including a €6 million fine against PricewaterhouseCoopers Business Solutions in 2020. Greek law includes specific provisions for processing employee data and special categories of sensitive information. Public sector data processing faces additional scrutiny, with the HDPA investigating government surveillance programs following the Predator spyware scandal that implicated senior officials.
laws.penalty: Administrative fines up to €20 million or 4% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher
exceptions: Processing for national security purposes with judicial authorization
Journalistic and academic research with appropriate safeguards
Vital interests of the data subject

quiz.q: What major scandal prompted increased HDPA scrutiny of government surveillance in Greece?
quiz.explanation: The Predator spyware scandal, which implicated senior Greek officials in surveillance of journalists and politicians, prompted intensified HDPA scrutiny of government data practices.

laws.title: Anti-Racism Law and Hate Speech Prohibition
laws.subtitle: Law 4285/2014 on racist violence and hate speech
laws.fullDescription: Greek Law 4285/2014 criminalizes public incitement to violence or hatred based on race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, and disability. The law increased penalties for racist crimes committed by organized groups and established hate crime as an aggravating factor in sentencing. Greece has faced EU criticism for inconsistent prosecution of racist violence against migrants, particularly following incidents in the Patras and Athens areas. The law was strengthened in 2019 to explicitly include antisemitic acts and Holocaust denial as criminal offenses.
laws.penalty: Imprisonment 3 months to 3 years; up to 5 years for offenses by organized groups
exceptions: Academic research and historical analysis
Artistic expression with legitimate purpose
Religious teaching within doctrinal limits

quiz.q: What additional element was added to Greece's anti-racism law in 2019?
quiz.explanation: In 2019, Greece strengthened Law 4285/2014 to explicitly criminalize antisemitic acts and Holocaust denial, following EU pressure to align with Framework Decision 2008/913/JHA.

laws.title: Foreign Direct Investment Screening
laws.subtitle: National security review of strategic sector investments
laws.fullDescription: Greece enacted Law 4894/2022 establishing an FDI screening mechanism in compliance with EU Regulation 2019/452, creating a mandatory review process for foreign investments in critical infrastructure, advanced technology, media, and defense. The Ministry of Development chairs an inter-ministerial committee that reviews qualifying investments within 35 working days. Greece designates its port infrastructure, particularly Piraeus (operated by China's COSCO), energy networks, and telecommunications as sensitive sectors requiring enhanced scrutiny. The law applies to investments from non-EU countries exceeding €1 million in strategic sectors.
laws.penalty: Blocking of non-compliant transactions; fines up to 10% of transaction value; forced divestiture
exceptions: Intra-EU investments not involving third-country beneficial owners
Portfolio investments below screening thresholds
EU-approved defense industry partnerships

quiz.q: Which Chinese company operates Greece's strategically important Port of Piraeus?
quiz.explanation: China's COSCO Shipping acquired majority control of the Port of Piraeus, making it a prominent example of foreign investment in Greek strategic infrastructure subject to screening.

laws.title: National Health System Reform Law
laws.subtitle: ESY restructuring post-austerity under Law 4486/2017
laws.fullDescription: Greek Law 4486/2017 restructured the National Health System (ESY) following severe cuts during the 2010-2018 austerity period that reduced the health budget by over 50%. The law merged hospital administrative functions, established hospital efficiency metrics, and created a new national primary care network. Greece implemented a universal healthcare coverage law in 2016 (Law 4368/2016) providing free access to uninsured residents for the first time. Despite reforms, Greece continues to have among the highest out-of-pocket health expenditure rates in the EU, at approximately 35% of total health spending.
laws.penalty: Healthcare professionals practicing without valid license: criminal charges; fines up to €30,000
exceptions: Emergency care must be provided regardless of insurance status
Chronic disease medications provided free for registered patients
Maternity care universally covered

quiz.q: What percentage of total health spending in Greece comes from out-of-pocket payments?
quiz.explanation: Greece has one of the EU's highest out-of-pocket health expenditure rates at approximately 35%, reflecting the impact of austerity cuts on the public health system.

laws.title: University Asylum Law Repeal
laws.subtitle: End of academic sanctuary under Law 4777/2021
laws.fullDescription: Greece repealed its controversial university asylum law in 2019 (Law 4619/2019) and subsequently enacted Law 4777/2021 establishing University Police units on campuses. The original asylum dating from 1982 had prohibited police entry onto university grounds, originally protecting students from military junta-era repression. Critics argued the asylum had been exploited by criminal elements and political extremists using campuses as sanctuaries. The University Police, a specialized unit of the Hellenic Police, became operational in 2021 and has faced both criticism from student unions and praise from university administrators concerned about campus safety.
laws.penalty: Trespass and disorder on campus: criminal charges; expulsion from educational institution
exceptions: Faculty and student demonstrations protected under freedom of assembly
Academic freedom in research and teaching
Student union activities within legal framework

quiz.q: What historical reason led to the original 1982 Greek university asylum law?
quiz.explanation: The 1982 university asylum law was enacted to protect students and academics from the kind of repression experienced under Greece's military junta (1967-1974).

laws.title: Same-Sex Civil Partnership Recognition
laws.subtitle: Cohabitation agreements for same-sex couples under Law 4356/2015
laws.fullDescription: Greek Law 4356/2015 extended civil partnership cohabitation agreements (symbiossi) to same-sex couples, granting most rights of married couples including inheritance, tax benefits, and hospital visitation rights. However, same-sex couples were explicitly excluded from adoption rights in the original law, a provision that faced legal challenges. In January 2024, Greece became the first Orthodox-majority country to legalize same-sex marriage and allow same-sex couple adoptions under Law 5089/2024, overriding opposition from the Greek Orthodox Church. The law passed with cross-party support under Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis.
laws.penalty: Discrimination against same-sex couples in provision of services: fines up to €5,000 per violation
exceptions: Religious ceremonies remain at discretion of clergy
Private clubs with religious affiliation may have limited exemptions
Foreign same-sex marriages recognized for residency purposes

quiz.q: What distinction did Greece achieve in January 2024 regarding LGBTQ+ rights?
options: First EU country to legalize same-sex marriage
First Orthodox-majority country to legalize same-sex marriage
First Balkan country to recognize civil unions
First Mediterranean country to ban conversion therapy
quiz.explanation: In January 2024, Greece became the first Orthodox-majority country in the world to legalize same-sex marriage and adoption rights, passing Law 5089/2024.

laws.title: E-Government and Digital Document Authentication
laws.subtitle: Digital transformation under Law 4727/2020
laws.fullDescription: Greek Law 4727/2020 on Digital Governance established the legal framework for electronic public services, digital identity, and the gov.gr platform. Citizens can now access over 1,400 government services online, obtain certified digital copies of documents, and conduct administrative procedures without physical attendance. The law implements EU eIDAS Regulation (910/2014) for electronic signatures and identity verification. Greece's digital transformation program, backed by Recovery and Resilience Facility funds, aims to fully digitize public administration by 2025, with the myCreditRisk and myAADE platforms representing significant milestones.
laws.penalty: Misuse of digital identity credentials: criminal charges under computer fraud law; fines up to €100,000
exceptions: Paper documents remain valid for those without digital access
Assisted digital services available at Citizen Service Centers (KEP)
Foreign nationals may use national eID equivalents

quiz.q: How many government services are accessible through Greece's gov.gr digital platform?
quiz.explanation: Greece's gov.gr platform provides access to over 1,400 government services online, part of the country's EU-funded digital transformation program.

laws.title: Wildfire Prevention and Urban Planning Law
laws.subtitle: Post-Mati disaster forest fire legislation
laws.fullDescription: Following the deadly 2018 Mati wildfire that killed 102 people, Greece enacted Law 4663/2020 establishing a National Civil Protection Authority and strengthening wildfire prevention requirements. The law mandates property owners in fire-risk zones to clear vegetation within 10 meters of structures and comply with updated Urban Planning Code restrictions prohibiting construction in previously burned forest land for 50 years. Drone surveillance and satellite monitoring are now systematically deployed during high-risk periods. The 2023 Evros wildfires, among Europe's largest recorded, prompted further emergency legislation on firefighting resources and cross-border EU coordination.
laws.penalty: Failure to clear vegetation: fines €1,500-€3,000; illegal construction in burned areas: criminal prosecution
exceptions: Agricultural land with approved fire management plans
Heritage buildings with alternative protection measures
Reforestation projects approved by Forestry Service
laws.sourceLabel: Greek General Secretariat for Civil Protection

quiz.q: How many people were killed in the 2018 Mati wildfire that prompted Greece's major fire safety legislation?
quiz.explanation: The 2018 Mati wildfire killed 102 people, making it Greece's deadliest wildfire disaster and prompting significant legislative reforms including Law 4663/2020.

laws.title: Asylum and Reception Conditions Law
laws.subtitle: Law 4636/2019 implementing EU asylum acquis
laws.fullDescription: Greek Law 4636/2019 consolidated the national asylum framework in line with EU Directives 2011/95 and 2013/33, establishing the Asylum Service as an independent administrative authority. The law governs reception conditions at Registration and Identification Centers (hotspots) on the Aegean islands, which have faced sustained criticism from UNHCR and NGOs for overcrowding and inadequate facilities. Greece received approximately 1.5 million irregular migrants between 2015-2016 at the height of the refugee crisis. The 2023 EU Migration Pact, supported by Greece, aims to redistribute processing responsibilities across member states.
laws.penalty: Illegal entry: administrative detention up to 18 months; accelerated border procedure for manifestly unfounded claims
exceptions: Unaccompanied minors subject to special protection procedures
Recognized refugees entitled to 3-year residence permit
Family reunification applicants with EU resident sponsors

quiz.q: Approximately how many irregular migrants did Greece receive during the 2015-2016 refugee crisis peak?
quiz.explanation: Greece received approximately 1.5 million irregular migrants between 2015-2016, making it the primary EU entry point during the European refugee crisis.

laws.title: Human Smuggling and Trafficking Law
laws.subtitle: Law 4198/2013 on combating trafficking in human beings
laws.fullDescription: Greek Law 4198/2013 implemented EU Directive 2011/36 on trafficking in human beings, establishing comprehensive criminal provisions and victim protection mechanisms. Greece's geographic position makes it a primary transit route for smuggling networks operating through the Aegean and Ionian Seas. The law criminalizes recruitment, transportation, and exploitation with penalties up to 10 years imprisonment, increased to 15 years when victims are minors. A National Rapporteur on Trafficking monitors trends and coordinates governmental response, though NGOs have criticized insufficient victim identification and support services.
laws.penalty: Imprisonment 5-10 years and fines; 10-15 years when victims are children; life imprisonment for organized criminal groups causing death
exceptions: Victims who assist prosecution may receive temporary residence permits
Humanitarian organizations providing legal assistance are protected
Undercover police operations authorized with judicial approval
laws.sourceLabel: National Commission for Human Rights Greece

quiz.q: What EU directive did Greece's Law 4198/2013 implement regarding human trafficking?
quiz.explanation: Greek Law 4198/2013 implemented EU Directive 2011/36 on preventing and combating trafficking in human beings and protecting victims.

laws.title: Investment Licensing Fast-Track Law
laws.subtitle: Strategic investment classification under Law 4864/2021
laws.fullDescription: Greek Law 4864/2021 established an accelerated licensing process for strategic investments exceeding €75 million (or €30 million in specific sectors), creating a one-stop-shop at Enterprise Greece, the investment promotion agency. Strategic investments receive an assigned coordinator, parallel processing of permits, and a binding 45-day response timeline for all required authorizations. The law also created a "National Champion" category for transformative investments in green energy, tourism, and technology. Since inception, the framework has facilitated approximately €15 billion in approved strategic investments including Microsoft and Google cloud infrastructure projects.
laws.penalty: Misrepresentation in strategic investment applications: disqualification and recovery of tax incentives with interest
exceptions: All investment sizes eligible for standard licensing which has separate timelines
Non-strategic investments use regular permitting through digital portal
EU-funded projects may follow alternative ESPA procedures

quiz.q: What is the minimum investment threshold to qualify as a 'strategic investment' under Greek Law 4864/2021?
quiz.explanation: Greek Law 4864/2021 sets €75 million as the general threshold for strategic investment status (€30 million in certain sectors), granting accelerated licensing benefits.

laws.title: Non-Performing Loan Securitization Scheme
laws.subtitle: Hercules Asset Protection Scheme for bank bad loans
laws.fullDescription: Greece established the Hercules Asset Protection Scheme (HAPS) under Law 4649/2019, a state-guaranteed securitization program enabling banks to offload non-performing loans (NPLs) that had reached 45% of total loans at their peak — the highest ratio in the EU. The scheme provides government guarantees on senior tranches of NPL securitizations, with banks retaining junior tranches to ensure alignment of interest. HAPS was extended twice and facilitated over €50 billion in NPL transfers by 2023, reducing the ratio to approximately 8%. The scheme was approved by the European Commission as compatible with state aid rules.
laws.penalty: Banking institutions failing to meet NPL reduction targets face enhanced supervisory measures and capital requirements
exceptions: State guarantees apply only to investment-grade senior tranches
Banks must retain economic interest in securitized portfolios
Guarantees expire if senior notes not repaid within guarantee period

quiz.q: What was the peak ratio of non-performing loans in Greek banks that prompted the Hercules scheme?
quiz.explanation: Non-performing loans reached 45% of total loans in Greek banks — the highest in the EU — prompting the Hercules Asset Protection Scheme established under Law 4649/2019.

laws.title: Electoral Law and Party Financing Reform
laws.subtitle: Law 4255/2014 on political party transparency
laws.fullDescription: Greek Law 4255/2014 regulates political party financing, requiring disclosure of donors above €100, prohibiting anonymous donations, and establishing the Parliament's Special Permanent Committee as overseer of party accounts. The law was strengthened after the Greek financial crisis exposed links between political financing and corruption in public procurement. Party accounts are audited annually by the Court of Auditors with results published. Greece's electoral system uses reinforced proportionality with a bonus-seat mechanism for the leading party, amended multiple times — most recently in 2023 to restore a proportional representation element after the Mitsotakis government initially proposed changes.
laws.penalty: Illegal party financing: disqualification from state subsidy; fines up to 3x the illegal amount; criminal prosecution of party officials
exceptions: Membership fees exempt from donation disclosure requirements
Proceeds from party publications and events treated separately
EU party group transfers follow separate European Parliament rules

quiz.q: What Greek institution audits political party accounts annually under Law 4255/2014?
quiz.explanation: The Court of Auditors (Elegktiko Synedrio) audits Greek political party accounts annually, with results published as part of the transparency framework.
